content: Sida cordifolia, a plant belonging to the Malvaceae family, is widely utilized in Ayurvedic medicine and is commonly referred to as Country Mallow or Bala. It thrives in transitional or waste areas. The leaves of this plant are heart-shaped, with one leaf growing at each node. Its flowers, which are yellow, are produced at the growing tips of the plant. The herb is characterized by its cooling, astringent, and intensely bitter properties, which make it effective in reducing inflammation. Additionally, it has diuretic and invigorating effects. In Ayurvedic medicine, Sida cordifolia is particularly beneficial for conditions associated with an imbalance in pitta dosha. It is known to rejuvenate the nervous, circulatory, and urinary systems. The root of Sida cordifolia has been used for over 2,000 years in the treatment of asthma and arthritis. Cooked leaves of the plant are traditionally used as a remedy for piles. In Cambodia, the roots are regarded as diuretic and depurative agents and are employed in the treatment of gonorrhea and ringworm. Bala is also incorporated into massage oils, which are applied topically to alleviate sore muscles and joints, particularly in conditions such as arthritis, rheumatism, sciatica, and neuritis affecting the legs. The leaves can be prepared as an infusion to manage fevers and delirium. The root of Sida cordifolia exhibits astringent, diuretic, and tonic properties. Its infusion is considered beneficial for conditions such as cystitis, strangury, hematuria, bleeding piles, chronic dysentery, leucorrhea, and gonorrhea. The seeds of the plant are believed to have aphrodisiac and nervine properties and are used in the treatment of colic, tenesmus, and gonorrhea. The plant contains several active constituents, including ephedrine (approximately 1%), phytosterols, and potassium nitrate. The phytosterols may exert an estrogenic effect. Sida cordifolia is included in certain weight-loss supplements, particularly after the ban on ephedra. These supplements typically contain 1% ephedrine alkaloid, which can assist in fat loss. This property makes it popular among bodybuilders and athletes seeking enhanced performance and a leaner physique. Currently, it is most commonly manufactured in tablet form, often combined with caffeine. Its effects on the body differ from those of Ma Huang, a well-known but controversial ephedra extract. While Ma Huang is a warmer herb, Sida cordifolia is more suitable for individuals with a hot constitution rather than a cold one. Like its relatives, Ma Huang and pseudoephedrine, Sida cordifolia is effective as an anti-asthmatic agent. It is also considered diaphoretic, diuretic, and a central nervous system stimulant. The Sida cordifolia plant is native to India, Cambodia, and Sri Lanka.
